To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the developmental appearance of the ammonia‐metabolising enzymes glutamine synthetases (GS) and carbamoyl‐phosphate synthetases I (CPS) in the liver is heterochronous, i.e., the two enzymes start to accumulate in different hepatocyte populations at different developmental stages, 2) the developmental appearance in the liver of GS and CPS is heterogeneous in that hepatocytes at the onset of enzyme appearance are not homogeneous in their enzyme content,
the developmental appearance of GS and CPS in the mouse liver is different from that in the rat liver.

in prenatal murine hepatocytes: (a) glutamine synthetases protein accumulation starts at embryonic day 15, first in hepatocytes around the major hepatoic veins, and (b) carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I protein accumulates first in the central hepatocytes of the median and the lateral lobes, and temporarily not at the peripheral hepatocytes and the caudate lobes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of the genes coding for ammonia‐metabolising enzymes during liver development.
the expression of enzymes of ammonia metabolism in the liver and small intestine during development.
the developmental appearance of enzymes involved in ammonia metabolism in the prenatal liver and small intestine of the mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developmental appearance of GS and CPS in mouse liver is characterized by a heterochrony and heterogeneity between hepatocytes, but that this is followed by the appearance of zonal heterochrony.

the expression of GS and CPS proteins in the mouse liver is initiated at ED 15, and that the initial phase of expression is characterized by a heterochronic and heterotopic expression of the enzymes, and by a heterogeneity between hepatocytes.
the developmental appearance of ammonia‐converting enzymes in the liver and small intestine is characterized by a heterochrony and heterogeneity in enzyme accumulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the developmental expression of the enzymes involved in ammonia metabolism in mammalian liver is characterized by heterogeneity in enzyme expression between hepatocytes, heterochrony in enzyme expression, and a heterochrony‐like pattern of expression of the two enzymes in the small intestine.

the developmental expression of GS and CPS in the mouse liver is characterized by a temporal heterogeneity in the enzyme content between hepatocyte subpopulations and by a spatial heterogeneity in the distribution of enzyme‐positive hepatocyte subpopulatons.
the expression of GS and CPS in the developing liver and small intestine is regulated at the level of protein accumulation, and that the expression of the enzymes is regulated independently.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developmental appearance of the ammonia‐metabolising enzymes is species dependent.
GS and CPS are not expressed in all hepatocytes simultaneously, and that the heterochrony in their appearance is species‐specific.
there is heterochrony in the appearance of ammonia‐utilizing enzymes in the mouse liver and small intestine.
